title: Model 30 highest_reliability doesn't work
description:
When a candidate route lacks an exact historical match, Model 30 estimates every candidate using the same aggregate neighbor evidence. That flattens success and cost estimates across routes; despite highest_reliability nominally sorting by success, the candidates tie and the cheap/default route wins.

The Hokusai fix should:

- Produce route-specific success and cost estimates for fallback candidates.

- Filter candidates by max_cost_usd before ranking.

- Select highest_reliability by highest estimated_success_under_budget, with deterministic tie-breakers.

- Preserve lowest_cost as the cheapest feasible candidate.

- Emit a diagnostic/warning and tradeoff spread when all objective routes genuinely collapse to the same route.

Wavemill needs only the companion compatibility work to retain that diagnostic in its route provenance.
